plan.summary: Anyone who was added to someone else's team will be able to leave it themselves from the team settings page. The team's owner cannot leave their own team, and nobody can leave their personal team.
acceptance_criteria: A signed-in member or admin of a team they do not own can leave it with a DELETE request to the route named team-membership.destroy, with the team as its parameter.
After leaving, the person is no longer in the team's member list and can no longer see or switch to that team.
If the team they left was their current team, their current team becomes their personal team.
The team's owner cannot leave the team they own; the request is refused (403) and they stay in it.
Nobody can leave their personal team; the request is refused (403).
A person who is not in the team cannot use the route for it; the request is refused (403) and nothing changes.
Guests are redirected to the login page.
Leaving a team only removes the person making the request; no other member is removed.
The team settings page shows a 'Leave team' button, with a confirmation dialog, to people allowed to leave, and hides it from the owner and on personal teams.
After leaving, the person is redirected (to the dashboard) with a success message.
assumptions: The owner may not leave their own team, since a team must keep its owner; transferring ownership is out of scope.
No email or notification is sent to the owner or admins when someone leaves.
Leaving needs a confirmation dialog in the interface but not password confirmation.
After leaving, the person is redirected to the dashboard with a flash toast, following the existing flashToast pattern.
The route lives in routes/settings.php alongside the other team settings routes, behind the auth and verified middleware.
plan.current_behavior: People cannot remove themselves from a team. Only a team's owner or an admin can remove members from it (RemoveTeamMember through TeamMemberController). Everyone has a personal team and can switch between the teams they belong to.
preserve: Only the owner and admins can remove other members from a team.
The owner always stays in their team and keeps the owner role.
Only the owner and admins can change members' roles; members cannot.
Everyone keeps a personal team and can never be left without one.
People can still switch between the teams they belong to, and cannot switch to teams they are not in.
Only the owner and admins can rename the team.
Members can still see the teams they belong to.
Deleting an account and signing up (which creates a personal team) keep working as before.

review.summary: The change adds a way for admins and members to leave a team they do not own, as a DELETE request to the route named team-membership.destroy with the team as its parameter. A form request checks a new 'leave' policy, which refuses non-members, the owner and personal teams. An action removes only the person asking and, when the team they left was their current team, moves them to their personal team. They are then sent to the dashboard with a success message. The team settings page shows a 'Leave team' button with a confirmation dialog only to people allowed to leave. New feature tests cover every acceptance criterion. Every verification check passed, the protected acceptance tests did not apply, and no tests were deleted or weakened. The diff does not touch removing members, changing roles, renaming teams, switching teams or signing up, so the rules that must stay as they are still hold. No blocking issues.

changes.behavior: A 'Leave team' section on the team settings page
changes.before: The team settings page had no way for someone to take themselves out of a team.
changes.now: Admins and members of someone else's team see a 'Leave team' section with a warning and a button. Pressing it asks them to confirm before anything happens. The owner does not see it, and nobody sees it on their personal team.

changes.before: Only the team's owner or an admin could take someone out of a team. People could not leave on their own.
changes.now: An admin or member can leave a team they were added to. They disappear from the team's member list, can no longer see or switch to that team, and land on the dashboard with a message saying they left. Nobody else in the team is affected.

changes.behavior: Owners and personal teams cannot be left
changes.before: Leaving a team was not possible at all.
changes.now: The owner cannot leave the team they own, nobody can leave their personal team, and people outside a team cannot use the leave option for it. Each of these attempts is refused and nothing changes.

changes.before: Someone's current team only changed when they switched it themselves.
changes.now: If someone leaves the team they were working in, they are moved back to their personal team automatically. If they leave a different team, their current team stays the same.

data.account:
People can now leave a team they were added to. Changes:
- TeamPolicy::leave(): allowed only when the user is in the team, is not its owner, and the team is not a personal team.
- New action App\Actions\Teams\LeaveTeam: inside a DB transaction it detaches the user. If the team was their current team, it moves them to another team they belong to, preferring their personal team (same logic as RemoveTeamMember).
- New TeamMembershipController::destroy, authorized by the new TeamMembershipDestroyRequest (which calls the leave policy). It calls LeaveTeam for the signed-in user, flashes a success toast ('You left the team.') and redirects to the dashboard.
- Route DELETE settings/teams/{team}/membership named team-membership.destroy, in the auth+verified group of routes/settings.php. Wayfinder helpers were regenerated; they are gitignored.
- TeamController::edit now passes a top-level `canLeave` prop. Team.vue has a 'Leave team' section with a destructive button and a confirmation dialog that submits the DELETE. It only shows when canLeave is true, so it is hidden from the owner and on personal teams.
- tests/Feature/Teams/LeaveTeamTest.php (13 tests) covers: members and admins can leave; a current team falls back to the personal team; the current team is kept when leaving another team; a user cannot switch to a team they left; the owner gets 403; a personal team gets 403; a non-member gets 403 and nothing changes; a guest is redirected to login; only the requester is removed; and canLeave on the settings page.
- Updated .builder/capabilities/membership.md with the new rule, the 'Leave a team' behaviour and the new paths.
Checks: pint passed, phpstan passed with 0 errors, php artisan test passed (78 tests), npm run check (format and lint) passed, npm run types:check (vue-tsc) passed. Existing remove, role and owner rules are unchanged.

findings.summary: The project rule says what each role may do is set in one place (config/teams.php). The new 'leave' policy instead checks the Owner role directly in code. Who may leave works correctly, but it does not follow the config-driven permission pattern the other team abilities use.
The tests check the 'canLeave' page flag but not the button or confirmation dialog themselves. The frontend type check and lint passed, so the risk is low.
TeamMembershipDestroyRequest has an empty rules() method. That is harmless because the request takes no input, but the method could carry a short comment saying so.
The verification run is labelled 'unverified' because no protected acceptance tests apply to this change. All the checks that did run passed.
